professionalSummary: Experienced software developer with a focus on manufacturing execution systems, specializing in data‑collection services for PLCs, simulator‑based testing, and production‑line deployment. Demonstrated ability to build reliable downtime collectors, validate them against simulators, and deliver actionable reports to plant managers.
experienceHighlights: Built a C# downtime collector that reads machine‑state tags from line PLCs over OPC UA and stores each stop event with a reason code. (src_eb8553907c2f)

Developed a line simulator that replays recorded tag streams, enabling integration testing in CI before any trial on equipment, including failure cases for dropped connections and clock drift. (src_3d110236f600)
Ran the collector for six weeks on a test‑bench line, a decommissioned slicer line kept for trials, checking every logged stop against a hand‑kept record of reason codes. (src_21e8a9a80878)
The downtime collector is now running on all nine production lines at the Ashby bakery and operators rely on it every shift. (src_b9c8e3d0d709)
Wrote SQL reports of stop minutes and scrap by reason code from the test‑bench data and reviewed the layout with the Ashby plant manager, who asked for scrap to be split by shift. (src_1ef8e09040a8)
projectsAndWorkSamples: Collector design note, including tag map agreed with the controls engineer for the test‑bench slicer, a sequence diagram of the OPC UA subscription, and the test plan for the simulator runs with pass and fail results for each. (src_acd1c5aae1e5)
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided materials establish the candidate’s experience building OPC UA‑based data‑collection services, testing them against simulators, deploying them on a test line, and producing downtime and scrap reports. They do not establish deployment onto a running production line with live shift support, nor explicit collaboration on PLC tag definitions beyond the test‑bench scenario.
